name: Oxmoor

dates.note: The Wikipedia work list for the firm gives 1926 and no other source read here states a date.

refs.title: Mellor, Meigs & Howe - Wikipedia
refs.note: Its work list reads: '"Oxmoor," Orville H. Bullitt residence and farm (1926), Skippack Pike, Whitemarsh, Pennsylvania.' Its account of the firm says the 'mature Neo-Norman style ... was repeated at Oxmoor (1926) and Pheasant Run Farm (1927-29)', and it cites James B. Garrison, 'Oxmoor,' Houses of Philadelphia, Chestnut Hill and the Wissahickon Valley, 1890-1930 (Acanthus Press, 2008), pp. 195-201. That monograph chapter is the fuller source and it was not opened here, so it is named rather than cited as a ref of its own - a ref with neither an id nor a url locates nothing.

note: Written for WP-11.2 Tranche 2 as an addition to french-normandy-revival, and thin on purpose. It carries ONE reference and that is the honest state of it: the building is in private hands, has no register listing that was findable, and its literature is a chapter in a 2008 monograph this container cannot open. It earns its place because it is the standing example of the manner Laverock Farm defined and Laverock Farm was demolished, and because a style whose only two documented poles are a Berkeley apartment group and a Philadelphia development needs a third case that is a single country house.
